prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood): auto start per demand/channel depth; permissives suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; blocked on low channel level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock; lost permissive->alarm/stop; maintenance release after isolations tagged, verified, acknowledged in shift turnover. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner; high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket to Laboratory Technician; trim from verified analyzer. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt). South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note. Chlorine Contact Basin: contact time per rate/level/residual. Clearwell Level Controller: storage limits; low-level interlock blocks pumps; high alarm; sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit after control system verifies level/isolation; trends vs filter production/demand. High Service Pump Header (Juniper): sequences pumps avoiding short cycling/unstable curve; lead/lag rotated by runtime, availability, Chief Operator restrictions; paced pressure control; produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip on threshold; on trip evaluates remaining pumps before starting another; supports North/South Distribution Pressure Stations via coordinated setpoints. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow): sends Jar Test Photograph Set. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern): time-sync master; audit; stores residual/level/pressure/pump data for event reconstruction. Actors: Chief Operator (modes, targets, dose, Storm Intake Mode); Duty Engineer (must review abnormal clearwell level, residual loss, header pressure loss, conflicting instruments before out-of-range setpoints); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip); Maintenance Planner (Quarry); Distribution Dispatcher (Falcon; communicates demand changes, main breaks, pressure complaints); Chemical Supplier Driver (sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log); Residuals Hauler. Chlorine Residual Alarm: pauses maintenance, grab sample, holds production increase. Return to service: evidence, bypasses removed, failed test keeps work order open; disinfection normal after Chief Operator confirms in Lantern. Modes: Automatic; Manual (only if operator maintains residual, clearwell limits, pressure with direct observation); return to Automatic needs stable residual, clearwell, pressure control for Chief Operator-set period; Storm Intake Mode (re-review work; watch

New part:
S150: Backwash recovery operation begins when the North Filter Gallery or South Filter Gallery completes a backwash cycle and the control system confirms that turbidity, valve position, and flow indications are within the expected recovery range.
S151: The Backwash Recovery Tank receives spent washwater under controlled conditions so that recovered water can be returned only after solids have settled and the operator has verified acceptable clarity.
S152: The SCADA Historian Server records recovery volume, tank level, turbidity trend, and return timing for each backwash recovery event.
S153: The Chief Operator uses the Filter Run Exception Note to determine whether a shortened run, high headloss, or abnormal turbidity response requires follow-up before the next wash sequence.
S154: When recovery water quality is outside the operating band, the Chief Operator holds the return path out of service and keeps the Backwash Recovery Tank in a settle-and-decant condition.
S155: The Duty Engineer reviews repeated abnormal wash recovery trends to determine whether the condition is hydraulic, chemical, instrumentation related, or caused by rapid source water change.
S156: Storm Intake Mode is used when runoff or river disturbance is expected to increase solids loading at the River Intake Pump Station and Raw Water Screen Channel.
S157: During Storm Intake Mode, operators monitor influent turbidity, screen differential level, coagulant demand, and filter headloss more frequently than during normal raw water conditions.
S158: The Coagulant Dosing Skid adjusts feed response only within approved operating limits and does not substitute automatic changes for required operator review during a significant upset.
S159: The Coagulant Dosing Skid uses the set to confirm the selected dose response during an event with rapidly changing raw water quality.
S160: Marigold shall hold the last operator-approved dose if the supporting process quality indications become inconsistent or unavailable.
S161: The Laboratory Technician prioritizes turbidity, apparent color, alkalinity, and disinfectant residual checks when filtration performance changes during a storm-driven event.
S162: Results from the Laboratory Technician are compared with online readings before operators make a sustained change to coagulation or filter loading strategy.
S163: If the North Filter Gallery shows rapid headloss growth after a verified chemical adjustment, the operator may stagger wash timing to avoid simultaneous recovery surges.
S164: If the South Filter Gallery shows turbidity breakthrough or delayed ripening, the affected unit is kept out of normal production until the Chief Operator approves return to service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
